title: Speculative decoding runtime adaptor: routing, verifier, and graceful fallback
creator: Ravi Singh
description: Add a runtime adaptor that enables speculative decoding across the serving stack. The adaptor performs lightweight model routing to a low-cost speculative model for prefill+decode handoff, runs an acceptance verifier on speculative outputs, and triggers a transparent fallback to full decode when acceptance thresholds are not met. The work touches kernel selection hints, KV cache handling for speculative prefixes, prefill scheduling (to support prefix reuse), and telemetry for acceptance and fallback rates. Goals: 1) integrate a pluggable routing policy so policy engineers can configure when to apply speculation (by model pair, token budget, or client tier); 2) implement a verifier stage that computes an acceptance score (delta logprob, top-k overlap, or token-level mismatch heuristic) within the tight latency envelope; 3) ensure fallback is seamless and safe (no cache pollution, correct sequence ids, and accounting for billing/metrics); 4) expose rich metrics to Console for canary rollouts and SLO assessment.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a configurable routing policy endpoint (policies: always, heuristics-by-length, tiered-by-customer)
Speculative path completes verifier within the decode latency SLO for 95th percentile under baseline load
Fallback preserves exact final output semantics (decode from full model yields same tokens given same RNG/seed) or is flagged in logs when nondeterminism causes divergence
No KV cache corruption: speculative prefixes are isolated and dropped on fallback; memory overhead bounded by configurable cap
Console shows per-policy acceptance_rate, fallback_rate, avg_delta_latency, and cost_savings_estimate; canary rollout supports traffic % control
End-to-end integration tests simulate acceptance thresholds and validate billing attribution for speculative vs full decode
comments: 2026-03-01 - Ravi Singh: Kicked off spike to evaluate verifier heuristics. Benchmarked two acceptance signals: delta-logprob over tokens and token overlap (top-3). Delta-logprob is more robust across quantized models but requires extra kernel launches for per-token logprobs.

2026-03-03 - Ava Martinez: Implemented prototype routing shim that can pick a speculative model variant based on request headers (customer_tier, max_tokens). Router is pluggable; next step is connecting verifier and ensuring it runs in the same GPU context to avoid PCIe overhead.

2026-03-04 - Engine team PR #1428: initial verifier proto that computes running logprob using specialized kernels. Observed 8-12ms overhead on A10G for 512-token prefill; need micro-optimizations to meet 95th percentile budget.

2026-03-06 - Design review (Ava): Decided to isolate speculative KV cache in a per-request ephemeral allocator. On fallback, ephemeral cache is discarded and full-model decode requests rehydrate KV from main cache or recompute prefill as needed. Trade-off: additional memory transient but simplified correctness.

2026-03-07 - Performance note: Kernel selection needs to be aware of speculative flow: when verifier requires per-token logprobs, pick kernel path with fused logprob+softmax where available. Added 'speculative' hint to kernel selector to prefer fused kernels if model supports them.

2026-03-09 - QA: Added synthetic workload that toggles acceptance thresholds to force fallback hot-path. Found rare race where fallback and ephemeral cache cleanup overlapped with trace exporter causing a stale seq-id surface in logs; fixed by serializing cleanup hooks with request finalization.

2026-03-10 - Ops: Canary plan drafted: start at 1% traffic for low-risk customers, monitor acceptance_rate and fallback_rate for 48h, then increase to 10% if fallback_rate < 2% and 95p latency delta < 30ms. Dashboard link included in attachments.
